title: When do objects float?
question: If you change the weight, how deep does it sink?
steps: Drag the barrel into the water.
Let go and watch the force pushing up.
Change the weight and compare how deep it sinks in.
observe: See how the buoyancy grows as more of the volume is under water.

terms.name: Buoyancy
terms.description: The force with which water or air pushes a thing up.

terms.name: Density
terms.description: How much mass is packed into the same volume.

terms.name: Volume under water
terms.description: The volume of the part of a thing that is in the water.

law.title: Buoyancy
law.description: The more volume is under water, the bigger the force pushing up.

tip: Drag the orange barrel up or down with one finger into the water or above it and let go: it stays right there (0.05 m steps). The blue arrow is buoyancy, the red arrow is weight. Change the barrel's mass and volume and compare how deep it sinks in.
tip_short: Drag the barrel up or down and let go

predict.question: If Bread Cat rides the small barrel, will it float?
predict.reason: Bread Cat and the load are heavy, so the weight is bigger than the buoyancy. So the small barrel sinks.

stages.say: Water pushes a barrel in it upwards. This force is called **buoyancy**. The empty barrel is light, so buoyancy wins. So even the small barrel floats.
stages.win: Bob, bob! The small barrel floats!
stages.miss: Make the small barrel light and float it!

stages.text: What if Bread Cat rides the small barrel?
stages.say: Bread Cat and the load are heavy. The weight is bigger than the buoyancy, so the small barrel sinks.
stages.miss: Put Bread Cat on the small barrel!

stages.text: Change to the big barrel and carry Bread Cat to the rock!
stages.say: A big barrel pushes away a lot of water, so its buoyancy is big. So it floats even with Bread Cat on it.
stages.win: Whee! Bread Cat made it to the rock!

story.clue: The piece fell on the rock in the middle of the pond! Let's float a barrel and get across!
story.map_clue: Something sparkles on the rock in the pond!

kid.intro: This is the floating lab. Water pushes things in it upwards. This force is called **buoyancy**. The more water a barrel pushes away, the bigger the buoyancy. To get Bread Cat across to the rock, the barrel has to float. Change the barrel's size and the load!
kid.title: Float a barrel across to the rock!
kid.say: The deeper the barrel is in the water, the harder the water pushes it up. A big barrel pushes away a lot of water, so it floats even with Bread Cat on it.
kid.tip: Drag the barrel up or down and let go!

note.law: Water pushes the barrel up as much as the volume under water. It floats when the buoyancy equals the weight.
